# Independent audit: aligned-simplex volume credit and critical-cap margin

Audited source:
`candidate eb88c1c4c388daab`.
This audit concerns its explicitly aligned simplex-middle branch, not
arbitrary mixed-integer bodies. The geometric theorem and saved critical
margin proof PASS. The final saved all-dimensional Section4 has also been read in full
and independently passes: its covariance conditioning remains in the
original barycentric law, its logarithmic derivative has the correct
sign, its finite rho values and exact top-three cancellations are
correct, and its statement retains every shape and criticality hypothesis.

## 1. Finite symmetry and ordinary volume

The map x ->((1-v_i.x)/(d+1))_i is an affine bijection from the
continuous d-space to the barycentric hyperplane. Its vertex coordinate
values show directly that coordinate permutations induce every simplex
automorphism. These automorphisms fix the centroid zero, hence are
linear. They map T onto itself, so change of variables gives absolute
determinant one. No Euclidean orthogonality is required. The group
acts transitively on the support normals by transpose/precomposition;
every normal appears equally often in the Minkowski-average support sum.
Therefore the averaged body B_* has each support h_(-v_i) equal to
m=(sum h_B(-v_i))/(d+1), and B_* is contained in both T and -mT.
Repeated ordinary BM gives |B_*|>=|B|. For an interior point of B,
each support strictly exceeds its corresponding point value; summing
uses sum v_i=0 and proves m>0. These steps preserve and track the
ordinary continuous fiber measure. They do not replace the actual
mixed source by B_*.

## 2. Opposite dilations, support signs, and sharpness

For L_t=tT intersect (-(1-t)T), averaging membership in each dilation
gives (L_s+L_t)/2 subset L_((s+t)/2). Each L_t is full dimensional
for 0<t<1. Reflection gives L_(1-t)=-L_t, so BM places their common
volume below |L_(1/2)|. Taking t=1/(1+m) yields the stated normalized
intersection bound, with exactly the factor((1+m)/2)^d.

For K={v_i.x>=-t_i}, the vector(r-t_i)_i has coordinate sum zero,
where r=mean t_i. Rank d makes it v_i.p for one unique p. Substitution
x=p+y gives K=p+r(-T). If r<0 the inequalities are inconsistent; if
r=0 they force a point; full dimension therefore gives r>0. Its exact
support h_K(-v_i)=t_i has the correct sign. Midpoint containment gives
2t_i>=h_A(-v_i)+h_B(-v_i). A proper cut v_i.x=-1 supplies
h_A(-v_i)>1, so r>(1+m)/2 strictly. Combining the two volume bounds
proves |K|>|B|/rho_d.

The sharp infimum example uses actual convex bodies
B=T intersect(-T), A_e=(1+e)(-T), K_e=(1+e/2)(-T). Every A cut
is proper, B is contained in -T, and Minkowski addition gives the
required midpoint inclusion. Its volume ratio tends to1/rho_d.
This establishes geometric sharpness only; the source does not claim
that these caps are depth-minimizing in that family.

## 3. The exact dimension constants

The added inequalities -mT are precisely
lambda_i<=(1+m)/(d+1). For j chosen violated coordinates, subtraction
of this common threshold leaves a translated simplex of scale
1-j(1+m)/(d+1), when positive. Its d-volume ratio is that scale^d;
nonpositive scales contribute zero. The boundaries have zero ordinary
d-volume, including the scale-zero case since d>=1. Inclusion-exclusion
therefore proves the source formula without an implicit Hausdorff or
Jacobian factor: numerator and denominator use the same affine chart.

The independently recomputed values are

    rho1=1, rho2=2/3, rho3=1/2, rho4=46/125,
    rho5=22/81, rho6=3364/16807, rho7=151/1024.

## 4. Genuine criticality and the profile prerequisites

At the actual source(0,0), every listed cap has a nonzero continuous
normal, so all fiber boundary hyperplanes are volume-null. All A cuts
are proper by hypothesis; all middle cuts are proper because0 is in
int K. B subset T makes its captured d-volumes zero. Hence the common
critical mass identity is exactly q_i=Q-U_i.

The A traces v_i.x>=-1 cover their entire continuous space, as do the
middle traces v_i.x>=0, by sum_i v_i=0. Thus ordinary positive-part
profiles apply to both ACTUAL bodies. The removal proof preserves
convexity and cap continuity, and its centroid invocation is ordinary
Grünbaum only. In the first source formula, alpha=Q-w is positive;
alpha=u is nonnegative. The coefficient d+1-1/Gamma is nonnegative
by the elementary Bernoulli bound, including d=1.

The finite integer-tilt equalization is legitimate because there are
only three bounded positive fibers and the continuous normal stays
nonzero. The endpoint masses vary continuously from(a,0) to(0,b),
with both extremes attained at finite tilts. The equal captured masses
t,t have their actual midpoint in the unchanged middle cap; q>=t by
BM when t>0 and trivially if t=0. Criticality gives U_i<=2t<=2q_i,
so U_i<=2Q/3. No existence of a guessed rounded centroid is used.

If the source is globally deepest, the middle centroid is an actual
comparison point, and all of its containing ambient halfspaces capture
at least Gamma k from K. Purely integer normals contain that entire
fiber. Thus Q>=Gamma k; the proof also correctly allows that explicit
comparison instead of global maximality. Geometric credit then gives
b<rho_d Q/Gamma, with a strict inequality.

The original all-d bound

    Q/M>3Gamma/[1+2(d+1)Gamma+3rho_d]

follows with the stated sign. In d=3 it is81/376, whose difference from
27/128 is27/6016 and whose ratio to27/128 is48/47. The saved source
correctly does not claim that this weaker general formula closes d>=4.

## 5. Independent top-three refinement

For d>=2, write kappa=1/Gamma-2 in(0,1), sort U_1<=...<=U_m,
and put m=d+1. Applying the ordinary profile at the third largest
cap yields exactly

    a<=U_m+U_(m-1)+kappa U_(m-2),
    k<=Q/Gamma-U_1-U_2-kappa U_3.

With w=U_m, their excess over Q/Gamma is bounded as follows:

    d=2: (1-kappa)(U_3-U_1)<=(1-kappa)w;
    d=3: U_4+(1-kappa)U_3-U_1-(1-kappa)U_2
                                                <=(2-kappa)w;
    d=4: U_5+U_4-U_1-U_2<=2w;
    d>=5: excess<=(2+kappa)w=w/Gamma.

Each coefficient is nonnegative. Substituting w<=2Q/3 and
b<rho_d Q/Gamma gives the rigorously checked strict bounds

    d=2: Q/M>4/17;
    d=3: Q/M>81/376;
    d=4: Q/M>768/3589;
    d>=5: Q/M>Gamma/(5/3+rho_d).

For d=4, 1+rho4+4Gamma4/3=3589/1875, below2 by161/1875;
thus768/3589>Gamma4/2. The d=1 bound1/4 already follows from the
original profile proof. No top-three formula is applied with two caps.

## 6. Elementary uniform rho bound, independently checked

Put n=d+1 and c=2/n. Let X be uniform on the standard barycentric
simplex with n coordinates. Conditional on X_i=x, the remaining
coordinates are(1-x)Y with Y uniform on the(n-1)-coordinate simplex.
This follows directly from affine scaling of the conditional simplex.
For any selected subset J of those coordinates, the conditional
probability g(x)=P(X_j<=c for j in J | X_i=x) is nondecreasing in x.
The function f(x)=1_{x<=c} is nonincreasing. For an independent copy X_i',

    Cov(f(X_i),g(X_i))
      =E[(f(X_i)-f(X_i'))(g(X_i)-g(X_i'))]/2<=0.

Applying this to one event and the remaining selected events, and
iterating in the ORIGINAL n-coordinate law, gives

    rho_d<=P(X_1<=c)^n
           =[1-(1-2/n)^(n-1)]^n.

No independence or general negative-association theorem is assumed.
The marginal tail is(1-c)^(n-1), from a translated-simplex volume ratio.

For real x>2 set f0(x)=(x-1)log(1-2/x). Its derivative is

    f0'(x)=-integral_(x-2)^x ds/s +1/(x-2)+1/x>0.

The strict inequality is the trapezoid bound for the strictly convex
function1/s on an interval of length2. Hence
(1-2/n)^(n-1)>=1/8 for every n>=4. If n>=9,

    rho_d<=(7/8)^n<=(7/8)^9<1/3,

where the last comparison is the integer inequality
3*7^9=121060821<134217728=8^9. The explicit values for n=6,7,8
above give the same strict1/3 bound. Thus rho_d<1/3 for every d>=5.
Combined with Section5, this closes the stated ALIGNED-SIMPLEX middle
critical-cap branch in every d. It does not remove that shape hypothesis.

## 7. Final-source and verifier result

Read the completed Section4 in full after it was saved. PASS with no
mathematical repair required. The optional t=0 clarification in the
finite-tilt BM step has been incorporated into Section3. The verifier
`supporting computation verify_aligned_simplex_credit_audit_slab_recovery.py` independently
checks the exact rho values, dimension margins, sorted-profile algebra,
and determinants of finite permutation actions. These checks supplement
the complete classical arguments above; they do not replace them.
